en: The Apadāna of the Elder Abbhañjanadāyaka Suvaṇṇabibbohana-vagga, Chapter 4 I gave a salve for the eyes to the Buddha, the Great Sage, the one who brings happiness to all beings. Because of that deed, I was reborn in the world of the Thirty-three gods. There I dwelt for ten thousand years, enjoying divine splendor. Having passed away from that realm, I was reborn here in the human world. Possessing great wealth and abundant grain, I am now a wealthy householder. I have lived for eighty-four thousand years, and my life has been free from disease. My body is well-proportioned, with limbs that are perfectly formed; I am handsome, pleasing to behold, and endowed with a beautiful complexion. My hair is black and lustrous, and my teeth are white and even. My skin is smooth and golden-hued, like the color of refined gold. I am honored by kings and ministers, and I am respected by the people of the countryside. I am praised by the wise and esteemed by the virtuous. I am beloved by the multitude and always surrounded by followers. I am never oppressed by hunger or thirst, nor am I ever afflicted by cold or heat. I am free from all ailments and dwell in constant happiness. Because I gave that salve to the Buddha, the Great Sage, I have attained such a state of glory. May I, through this merit, attain the supreme state of Buddhahood. May I become a teacher of gods and men, a refuge for the world. May I cross over the ocean of saṃsāra and lead others across as well. May I attain the bliss of Nibbāna, the ultimate peace. Thus did I speak these verses of praise for the Elder Abbhañjanadāyaka. Of the Blessed One Koṇḍañña,
who is free from passion, such-like,
whose mind is equal to space—
For one who meditates without conceptual proliferation,
who has transcended all delusion,
and who seeks the welfare of the entire world;
Anointing ointment was given by me to the Lord of Bipeds, the Tathāgata,
immeasurable eons ago from now.
I experienced the intoxication of that ointment;
I do not recall ever falling into an evil rebirth—
this is the fruit of that ointment.
In this fifteenth aeon,
there was a kṣatriya named Cirappa,
who was endowed with the seven treasures.
A wheel-turning monarch of great power.
The four analytical knowledges... [and so forth].
“Such is the teaching of the Buddha.
Thus indeed the venerable elder Abbhañjanadāyaka spoke these verses.
This is the fourth *apadāna* of the elder Abbhañjanadāyaka.
